feedbackflow.metaDescription: FeedbackFlow — open-source alternative to Canny for collecting, prioritizing and delivering product feedback. Case study: context, problem, solution and technical decisions (Next.js 16, TypeScript, Prisma).
feedbackflow.title: FeedbackFlow
feedbackflow.lead: Collect, prioritize and deliver product feedback — an open-source alternative to Canny. A public voting space, a roadmap and a dashboard, designed to stay simple to self-host.
contexte: Tools like Canny are effective but closed and paid beyond minimal usage. I wanted a short-scoped project to demonstrate my ability to ship a complete, clean and deployable product — from the data schema to the public interface.
FeedbackFlow is therefore designed as a self-hostable building block: a team installs it, opens a feedback portal, and retains full control of their data.
feedbackflow.problemeIntro: Beyond the 'clone' concept, three constraints shaped the project:

problemePoints.label: Signal over noise.
problemePoints.body: Many submissions, little signal: a voting and status system is needed to surface what matters.

problemePoints.label: Two audiences, one codebase.
problemePoints.body: A public space for users, an admin back-office for the team — without duplicating logic.

problemePoints.label: Simple to deploy.
problemePoints.body: No exotic infrastructure: a Postgres database and a Vercel-type platform should be enough.

solutionBody: I split the product into three surfaces: a public portal (submit an idea, vote, track progress), a roadmap in columns by status, and a dashboard to sort, merge and evolve requests.
Everything is built on a single data model and server-side rendering (App Router) for fast, indexable public pages.

decisions.title: Server rendering for the public
decisions.body: Public pages (ideas, roadmap) are server-rendered: fast on first load and indexable by search engines.
decisions.why: SEO and speed are critical for an open feedback portal.

decisions.title: One schema, two uses
decisions.body: The same model (ideas, votes, statuses, comments) feeds both the public portal and the admin. Prisma secures queries with end-to-end typing.
decisions.why: Avoid logic duplication and inconsistencies between the two surfaces.

decisions.title: End-to-end typing
decisions.body: Shared types between the database, API and components: fewer silent bugs, confident refactors.
decisions.why: Ship fast without sacrificing reliability — the project's hallmark.

feedbackflow.resultatBody: A complete, open-source product deployable in minutes — that also serves as a concrete demonstration of how I work: clear scope, typed code, real production deployment.

linkforge.metaDescription: LinkForge — URL shortening API with authentication, API keys, asynchronous anonymized click tracking and analytics. Case study: context, problem, solution and technical decisions (Fastify, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ).
linkforge.title: LinkForge
linkforge.lead: A URL shortening API with authentication, API keys, asynchronous and anonymized click tracking, and analytics. Designed to stay fast and handle load, even when redirects pile up.
contexte: A URL shortener is a deceptively simple classic: easy to do badly, hard to do well. Behind a simple redirect lie questions of performance, security and audience measurement.
I wanted to make it a short-scoped but back-end demanding project: a real API, authenticated, instrumented, and designed to handle traffic without slowing down the redirect.
linkforge.problemeIntro: Three requirements shaped the entire architecture:

problemePoints.label: The redirect must stay instant.
problemePoints.body: Measuring a click must never slow down the user following the link.

problemePoints.label: Useful stats, without tracking.
problemePoints.body: Count and qualify clicks while anonymizing personal data.

problemePoints.label: Programmable and secure access.
problemePoints.body: Authentication and API keys to integrate the service elsewhere.

solutionBody: The core of the system separates the hot path (the redirect) from the cold path (analytics). On each click, the API immediately responds with the redirect and delegates click processing to a queue, consumed in the background.
Result: the end user never pays the cost of measurement, and statistics are built reliably, at their own pace.

solutionGallery.alt: Create a short link + API key

decisions.title: A framework built for speed
decisions.body: Fastify offers minimal per-request overhead: ideal for a service whose primary function is to respond fast, thousands of times.
decisions.why: Redirect latency is the product's #1 criterion.

decisions.title: Asynchronous click tracking
decisions.body: Each click is pushed into a BullMQ queue (on Redis) and processed outside the response path: enrichment, anonymization and aggregation happen in the background.
decisions.why: Decoupling measurement from redirection guarantees stable response times under load.

decisions.title: Durable & queryable data
decisions.body: Postgres stores links, API keys and aggregated statistics; Prisma secures access with strict typing shared across the API.
decisions.why: Reliable analytics require a solid relational database, not just a cache.

linkforge.resultatBody: A complete, documented API that concretely demonstrates how I approach back-end work: performance first, reliable measurement second, privacy by design.
